description: How a dev build gets past the sign-in screen without a mailbox in the way (docs/sign-in.md). 'account': the address a dev build offers to sign in as, so trying things out costs one press and never the owner's own account. Its code goes through the local stack's mailbox like any other address. 'mailbox': the mailbox behind a backend URL, where the local stack catches every message it sends, or null when the backend is not the local stack, which is the only place any build may read mail from or offer the dev account on. The stack serves its API on 55321 and its mailbox on 55324 over plain http (supabase/config.toml), so those two ports are the whole test. 'codes': the sign-in code inside a message, the first run of exactly six digits, or null when the message holds none.

mailbox.name: the local stack on this machine
the same stack as a phone on the network reaches it
the host as an emulator reaches it
a trailing slash is the same stack
the cloud project has no mailbox to read
https on the stack's port is not the local stack either
another port is not the stack
